title: Zariski main theorem after an admissible blowup
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Open and closed immersions mean representable morphisms whose scheme base changes have the indicated property [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], write $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T$ for the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal K^d$, constructed by etale descent of the ordinary scheme blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] on affine etale charts. Finite type means locally generated by finitely many sections. Let $f:X\to T$ be a separated finite-type morphism of algebraic spaces. Suppose $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $U\hookrightarrow T$ is a quasi-compact open subspace, and $X\times_TU\to U$ is an isomorphism. Then there is a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ with $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$ and an open immersion over $T$ $$v:\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_X}X\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}T,$$ where $\mathcal I\mathcal O_X=\operatorname{im}(f^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_X)$. Writing $b_X$ and $b_T$ for these blowup maps, one has $b_Tv=fb_X$. Under the canonical identifications of both inverse images of $U$ with $U$, the restriction of $v$ is the identity. No density of $U$ in $T$ and no properness or finite presentation of $f$ are assumed. Separatedness of $f$ cannot be dropped: for the affine line with doubled origin $X\to T=\mathbf A^1_k$ over a field $k$ and $U=\mathbf A^1_k\setminus\{0\}$, every such $\mathcal I$ is invertible, both blowups are the identity, and $f$ is not injective.

proof.text: Choose a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_0$ with $V(\mathcal I_0)$ having underlying set $T\setminus U$ and $\mathcal I_0|_U=\mathcal O_U$, by [lem-sfb-space-qc-open-boundary-ideal]. Put $p:T_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_0}T\to T$. Its exceptional ideal is Cartier and its complement is the copy of $U$, schematically dense in $T_1$, by [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties]. Take the strict transform $f_1:X_1\to T_1$ using [lem-sfb-space-strict-transform-as-blowup]. That statement gives $T_1$ qcqs and $f_1$ separated, finite type and quasi-separated, and identifies its restriction over $U$ with $X_U\to U$.

The open in $T_1$ identified with $U$ is quasi-compact. Over it $f_1$ is an isomorphism, hence flat and locally of finite presentation: after identifying domain and codomain, the map is the identity, witnessed by identity ring maps on a common etale atlas. Apply [lem-sfb-space-flattening-by-admissible-blowup] to $f_1$ and this open. Obtain $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_{T_1}$ of finite type, unit over $U$, and $q:T_2=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}T_1\to T_1$ such that the iterated strict transform $f_2:X_2\to T_2$ is flat and of finite presentation. By [lem-sfb-space-strict-transform-as-blowup] it is also separated.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-composition-centres-and-transforms] to $p,q$. Obtain $\mathcal L$ and $e:T_2\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L}T$ over $T$. The support formula gives $V(\mathcal L)=T\setminus U$ as sets: $V(\mathcal I_0)=T\setminus U$, while $V(\mathcal J)$ is disjoint from $p^{-1}U$. Thus $\mathcal L|_U=\mathcal O_U$. The same cited statement identifies $X_2$ with the strict transform of $X$ for this single blowup, with both projections preserved. By [lem-sfb-space-strict-transform-as-blowup] it is therefore $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L\mathcal O_X}X$.

source.place: Tags 0860 and 0868, including the support condition required by 0868.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties], the inverse image of $T\setminus V(\mathcal L)=U$ is schematically dense in $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L}T\cong T_2$. Its inclusion is quasi-compact: an affine etale chart has a finite affine cover trivializing the exceptional Cartier ideal; on each member its complement is a principal affine open, so the whole inverse image is a finite union of quasi-compact opens. The map $f_2$ is separated, flat and locally finite type, and is an isomorphism over this open by the off-centre restriction in [lem-sfb-space-strict-transform-as-blowup]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-flat-isomorphism-dense-open] to conclude that $f_2$ is an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 087F, final application of Tag 0879; density from Tags 085T and 083S.

proof.text: Set $\mathcal I=\mathcal L$ and use the projection-compatible identifications above to write $f_2$ as $v:\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_X}X\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}T$. Compatibility of the two projections gives $b_Tv=fb_X$. Over $U$ both blowup maps are isomorphisms and the identified morphism is $X_U\to U$; under its given isomorphism with $U$ the map is the identity. These are the required claims.
